messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED - incident_id=INC-2025-0896 - region: us-west-2 - type: multi-region failover triggered

Sanjay: paging - saw a big spike in 5xx from us-west-2 about 1749536000. Frontdoor started failing health checks, traffic shifted to us-east-1 but we're seeing elevated tail latency there (p95 -> 1.8s).

Marie: I'm on it, checking LB/route53. Can someone confirm if this is an AZ-wide networking blip or a control-plane thing?

Raj: I'm pulling VPC flow logs + CloudWatch metrics now. Early look: a bunch of connection resets in us-west-2a -> nat-gw-1 around 1749535900. Looks like an AZ-level routing flap.

Elaine: @sanjay can you post the curl check from the failing node? Need raw error.

Sanjay: paste:```\nHTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: text/html
X-Request-Id: 7a2f... 
Upstream error: connection reset by peer
```

Marie: Route53 health checks show origin failures for /health in us-west-2 for host redwood-app-ww-west-2.internal. Healthcheck failure rate ~35% since 1749535850. TTL currently 60s.

oncall-bot: Incident severity set to P1 (customers impacted). Paging page: #inc-ops, #oncall-sre, #cs-urgent.

cs-tim: Received two customer tickets: "latency spikes and 500s" from a PSP customer in EMEA and one enterprise in APAC. Let me know if we should trigger customer comms.

Nick: we're seeing consistent backend worker errors too, likely a cascade after the regional flaps. Checking autoscaler + pod restart events.

Raj: VPC route table shows intermittent withdrawal of a specific route to the AZ NAT gateway — looks like the cloud provider's internal routing had a transient BGP withdraw for a subset of hosts in us-west-2a.

Marie: Action plan: 1) Stop further automated cross-region failovers while we stabilize (disable automatic failover policy). 2) Manually shift only safe traffic (canary) to us-east-1. 3) Drain affected AZ instances in us-west-2a. 4) Notify customers about degraded performance.

Sanjay: I'm disabling autoswitch at the routing layer now:```\n# disable automated failover
redwoodctl routing update --auto-failover=false --region=global
```

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline blocked: auto-failover flag change detected. Confirm? (yes/no)

Elaine: yes, confirm. We can't have cascading shifts while routing is unstable.

Marie: Starting drain on nodes in us-west-2a: kubectl cordon/drain commands queued. Will keep one AZ healthy for local traffic if possible.

Nick: kubectl logs show frequent ECONNRESET from the database proxy in that AZ. Might be causing app worker retries -> 5xx. Could be dependent on underlying network flaps.

Raj: Provider status page: "We are investigating networking connectivity in us-west-2 AZ a". There's an open support ticket already. I've added our logs to the ticket.

Sanjay: For mitigation, enabling sticky routing to healthiest endpoints for 5 minutes to reduce churn. Also reducing DNS TTL to 10s to allow faster recovery when we re-enable failover. Command:```\naws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","TTL":10,"SetIdentifier":"global","Weight":1}}]}'
```

cs-tim: Sending interim note to affected customers now: "We're investigating a regional networking incident in us-west-2 causing intermittent 500s/latency. We have mitigation in place and will update in 30 mins." Will attach link to status page.

Marie: Observability note: Enabled deeper tracing on cross-region retries and increased sampling to 100% for the affected routes. If anyone adds spans, tag with incident=INC-2025-0896.

Elaine: Handoff: I've been monitoring since T+10m. Sanjay, need to sleep in 50m — can you take on-call after that? I'll compile an action checklist for the night shift.

Sanjay: I can take the handoff at 1800 UTC. For the handoff note: 1) auto-failover disabled, 2) nodes in us-west-2a cordoned & draining, 3) DNS TTL reduced to 10s, 4) provider has an open ticket.

Raj: Confirming cordon/drain finished on 3 of 4 node pools in us-west-2a. Mesh shows most traffic being served from us-west-2b + cross-region. Error rates in us-west-2 overall dropping from 32% -> 12% since drains began.

Nick: Observed a problematic healthcheck loop where failing nodes triggered failover for a subset of tenants, which then overloaded the target region. That's the cascade we feared. After disabling auto-failover, cache pressure in us-east-1 is stabilizing.

oncall-bot: NOTE: scheduled on-call handover at 1749537600. Handoff checklist required.

cs-tim: Customer update 2: "We're seeing improvement but intermittent 500s persist for some endpoints. Root cause seems to be a regional network issue." Customers asking for ETA. Suggest: ETA TBD pending provider fix; we're keeping them in the loop.

Marie: Provider reports partial remediation for internal routing at 1749536300. Recommend gradual re-enable of failover with strict rate limits and a canary to avoid re-triggering.

Sanjay: Re-enable auto-failover in canary mode (10% traffic) and monitor. Command:```\nredwoodctl routing update --auto-failover=canary --canary-weight=0.1
```

Nick: p95 in us-east-1 back to baseline after canary, error rate stable ~1-2%. If no regressions in 10 min we can widen to 50%.

Elaine: Post-mortem draft items: - Improve detection to avoid full-region failover based on single-AZ health signals - lower initial failover weight and add cooldown - add provider-specific alarms for route withdraw patterns - automate DNS TTL drop during incident to 5-10s - run DR failover dry-run quarterly

Sanjay: Agree on postmortem. Also add runbook: check for NAT/gateway withdraws and block auto-failover if AZ-level withdraw detected.

Marie: I'll keep this thread as the running incident log. Last update: provider says full routing stability restored at 1749536385. Continuing to monitor 30m.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring) - INC-2025-0896 - resolved_at=1749536385 - impacted_regions=us-west-2 (AZ a) - summary: provider networking flap caused AZ-level route withdraws leading to unhealthy failover cascade; mitigations: disabled auto-failover, drained AZ, reduced DNS TTL, canary re-enable.

cs-tim: Final customer note being sent: "Services returning to normal, actively monitoring, contact CS for any remaining issues."

Elaine: Action items assigned in triage board. I'll own the runbook update. Thanks team, great coordination. :clap:
